works.title: To Ablabius: That There Are Not Three Gods
works.summary: Gregory answers the charge that three persons sharing one nature are three gods, arguing from the unity of divine activity.
works.significance: A key text on inseparable operations and the unity of the Trinity.

works.title: Dialogue Against the Luciferians
works.summary: A dialogue arguing that bishops who signed the Homoian creed of Ariminum (359) under pressure should be received back, against the rigorist followers of Lucifer of Cagliari.
works.significance: Contains Jerome's famous description of the Arian ascendancy in 359.

works.title: On the Trinity (De Trinitate)
works.summary: Fifteen books (c. 400–420): the scriptural basis of the Trinity, the logic of relations, and analogies of the Trinity in the human mind (memory, understanding, will).
works.significance: The most influential Western work on the Trinity; basis of the Filioque and of scholastic Trinitarianism.

works.title: Mystagogy of the Holy Spirit
works.summary: Photius' systematic case against the Filioque: biblical, patristic and logical arguments that the Spirit proceeds from the Father alone.
works.significance: The classic Byzantine statement against the Filioque.

works.title: Summa Theologiae
works.summary: Thomas Aquinas' unfinished synthesis of Christian theology (1265–1274): God, creation, the moral life, Christ and the sacraments.
works.significance: The central text of scholastic theology; foundational for Catholic teaching on God, simplicity, the Trinity as relations, grace and the Eucharist.

works.title: Racovian Catechism
works.author: Polish Brethren (Socinians)
works.summary: The confession of the Minor Reformed Church of Poland, published at Raków: one God the Father, Jesus a man raised to divine authority, rejection of satisfaction atonement.
works.significance: The classic statement of Socinian antitrinitarianism, influential in Dutch and English rationalism.

works.title: Unitarian Christianity (Baltimore sermon)
works.summary: Channing's ordination sermon for Jared Sparks in Baltimore, setting out rational interpretation of Scripture, the unity of God, the unity of Christ and the moral perfection of God.
works.significance: The manifesto of American Unitarianism.

works.title: Process and Reality
works.summary: Whitehead's Gifford Lectures (1927–28) presenting a metaphysics of actual occasions and a dipolar God.
works.significance: Foundational text of process philosophy and theology.

quotes.text: Our teacher of these things is Jesus Christ… and that we reasonably worship Him, having learned that He is the Son of the true God Himself, and holding Him in the second place, and the prophetic Spirit in the third, we will prove.
For with Him were always present the Word and Wisdom, the Son and the Spirit, by whom and in whom, freely and spontaneously, He made all things.
By this Praxeas did a twofold service for the devil at Rome: he drove away prophecy, and he brought in heresy; he put to flight the Paraclete, and he crucified the Father.

…the mystery of the dispensation is still guarded, which distributes the Unity into a Trinity, placing in their order the three Persons—the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost: three, however, not in condition, but in degree; not in substance, but in form; not in power, but in aspect; yet of one substance, and of one condition, and of one power.
Origen argues that God was never without his Wisdom; the Son is begotten eternally, as brightness from light, so that there was no point at which the Son did not exist.
We are persecuted, because we say that the Son has a beginning, but that God is without beginning.
quotes.citation: Arius, Letter to Eusebius of Nicomedia, in Theodoret, Ecclesiastical History 1.4

quotes.text: For He was made man that we might be made God; and He manifested Himself by a body that we might receive the idea of the unseen Father.
quotes.translation: NPNF ser. 2 vol. 4, trans. A. Robertson

quotes.text: Athanasius argues that if the Son is the Father's own Word and Wisdom, then to say ‘there was once when He was not’ is to say God was once without reason and wisdom — and that the Father was not always Father.
The whole world groaned, and was astonished to find itself Arian.
The distinction between ousia and hypostasis is the same as that between the general and the particular; as, for instance, between the animal and the particular man.
quotes.translation: NPNF ser. 2 vol. 8, trans. Blomfield Jackson

quotes.text: No sooner do I conceive of the One than I am illumined by the Splendour of the Three; no sooner do I distinguish Them than I am carried back to the One.
quotes.translation: NPNF ser. 2 vol. 7, trans. Browne & Swallow

quotes.text: The Old Testament proclaimed the Father openly, and the Son more obscurely. The New manifested the Son, and suggested the Deity of the Spirit. Now the Spirit Himself dwells among us, and supplies us with a clearer demonstration of Himself.
quotes.translation: NPNF ser. 2 vol. 7, trans. Browne & Swallow
quotes.citation: Gregory of Nazianzus, Oration 31 (Fifth Theological Oration) 26

quotes.text: Gregory of Nyssa argues that because every divine action toward creation issues from the Father, proceeds through the Son and is perfected in the Holy Spirit as one single operation, the persons cannot be counted as three gods the way three human beings are counted as three men.
quotes.citation: Gregory of Nyssa, To Ablabius: That There Are Not Three Gods (paraphrase)

quotes.text: Now love is of some one that loves, and something is loved with love. Behold, then, there are three things: he that loves, and that which is loved, and love.
quotes.translation: NPNF ser. 1 vol. 3, trans. A. W. Haddan

quotes.text: Augustine admits that when asked ‘three what?’ human speech labours under great poverty; we say ‘three persons’ not in order to say something exact, but so as not to remain silent.

Photius argues that if the Spirit proceeded from both the Father and the Son, there would be two causes in the Godhead — or else the Father's distinctive property of being cause would be shared with the Son, confusing the persons and destroying the monarchy of the Father.
quotes.citation: Photius, Mystagogy of the Holy Spirit 4–11 (paraphrase)

quotes.text: Aquinas teaches that a divine person signifies a relation as subsisting: paternity is the Father, filiation the Son, procession the Holy Spirit — really distinct from one another, yet each identical with the one divine essence.
quotes.citation: Thomas Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I, q. 29, a. 4; q. 28 (paraphrase)

quotes.text: Channing holds that Scripture teaches the unity of God as one being and one person, and that the doctrine of three persons, each fully God, is irreconcilable with that unity and with the plain sense of the Bible.
quotes.citation: W. E. Channing, ‘Unitarian Christianity’ (1819), part II.1 (paraphrase)

quotes.text: Rahner's axiom: the Trinity revealed in the history of salvation (the ‘economic’ Trinity) is the Trinity as God is in himself (the ‘immanent’ Trinity), and vice versa.
quotes.citation: Karl Rahner, The Trinity (1967; ET 1970), ch. 1 (paraphrase)
